nodes.title: IDENTITY
nodes.label: IDENTITY
nodes.body: Jaguar / Panthera onca. Canonical species identity is carried by the SPECIES layer.
nodes.boundary: Identity does not establish local presence, population size or a live animal position.

nodes.title: RELATIONSHIP
nodes.label: PREY RELATIONSHIP
nodes.body: Capybara is a documented jaguar prey taxon in a bounded Southern Pantanal study context.
nodes.boundary: This does not imply the same dietary importance everywhere or diagnose an Amazon diet.

nodes.title: LIVING SYSTEM
nodes.label: CONNECTED HABITAT
nodes.body: Connected habitats can support movement, prey access and gene flow across jaguar populations.
nodes.boundary: Connectivity needs and population effects are landscape-specific and require local evidence.

nodes.title: PRESSURE → CAUSE
nodes.label: PRESSURE → CAUSE
nodes.body: Habitat loss and fragmentation are documented range-wide pressure categories for jaguars. The immediate cause class in this current evidence path is human-driven habitat conversion and fragmentation.
nodes.boundary: Local intensity, mechanism and population effect require place-specific evidence.

nodes.title: HOW DO WE SOLVE THIS?
nodes.label: HOW DO WE SOLVE THIS? →
nodes.body: Continue from pressure and cause into Solutions Intelligence. The XR lens should never stop at awareness.
nodes.boundary: Possible responses are not 4PLANET delivery claims.
